plans.note: No dedicated liability heading surfaced in the outline; scan the unnumbered body under the agreement title for a limitation/exclusion of damages provision and check mutuality, cap size and carve-outs (IP, confidentiality, gross negligence).

Look for HDI indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from the site/hosting deliverables and from HDI's misconduct; the access/content provisions in 1.4 may carry a reciprocal content indemnity from the Company that should stay narrow.
No restrictive-covenant section appears in the outline; confirm by scanning the body for any limit on the Company selling Deerskin Products through other channels or sites.

Site development and hosting deals often make HDI the sole provider of site services; check the scope-of-services language and 1.4 access terms for any obligation on the Company to source hosting or fulfilment only from HDI.
No pricing/most-favoured-customer heading in the outline; scan fee provisions for any promise by the Company to give HDI terms no less favourable than those given to others.

Personnel-related text is most likely near the appointment of representatives in 5.4; check there and in the general body for any hiring restriction binding the Company, and whether a general-advertising carve-out and time limit exist.

The defined term 'Termination Date' signals a term/termination provision in the body; verify whether the Company may terminate on notice without penalty and whether HDI has a matching mid-term exit that should be removed.
Check the term provision tied to 'Termination Date' for automatic renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any price uplift on renewal.
Boilerplate near the signature block; confirm governing law is NY/DE/CA/England and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration. Check the closing provisions preceding sec-p0072.

Look in the miscellaneous/boilerplate run before the signature block for assignment and change-of-control; ensure the Company may assign to affiliates and successors and HDI has no termination right on our change of control.

Section 1.4 (HDI providing the Company access) and the development provisions are the likely locus of ownership language for the site, deliverables and Company content/customer data; confirm no assignment of Company IP or data to HDI.
The access grant in 1.4 is the probable licence clause; test scope for affiliates and contractors, sublicensability and whether it is revocable at will by HDI.
No audit/records heading in the outline; scan fee and records provisions for any HDI right to inspect the Company's books, and check notice, frequency and cost allocation if found.
Check the fee/termination provisions for early-termination fees, penalties or liquidated damages payable by the Company; service credits running to us are acceptable.
Look for HDI warranties on development quality, site availability and non-infringement, plus any disclaimer of implied warranties; assess duration and remedy.
No insurance heading surfaced; given HDI hosts Company data, confirm absence in the body and flag as missing if there is no coverage obligation.
Scan the fee and services provisions for minimum spend, minimum volumes of Deerskin Products, or take-or-pay commitments binding the Company, and for any exit right.
Check the consequences-of-termination text keyed to 'Termination Date' for return of Company data/content, site migration and continued access under 1.4 during a wind-down period.
